newsitem.title: UK: Dollar mauls mark, Dow boosts Eurobourses.
newsitem.headline: Dollar mauls mark, Dow boosts Eurobourses.

text.p: The dollar rallied to a 34-month high against the mark on Tuesday on a combination of German unemployment gloom and U.S. economic optimism, and the bulls came out of hiding on European equity markets.

Heartened after Wall Street closed up following three consecutive tumbles; London, Frankfurt and Paris stocks all opened sharply higher and continued to firm in morning trading. Frankfurt put on more than 1.5 percent to sail through its previous trading peak.

Currency market analysts said there was little news overnight to account for the latest dollar push higher, but the yawning gap between 10-year U.S. and German bond yields, now 1.15 percentage points in favour of the dollar, was a major driving force.
"We feel dollar/mark has miles to go yet," said Peter Von Maydell, currency economist at UBS. The last time the bund/T-note spread was this wide was 1989 when dollar/mark was at 1.88.

By mid-morning the dollar had hit a peak of 1.7112 marks -- well up from its close in Europe on Monday at 1.6941 marks -- although it later drifted to just below 1.71. Against the yen it was also off its morning peak of 122.12. This compares with 120.92 late on Monday.
The dollar rally also subdued the mark in Europe against the lira and peseta.

Von Maydell at UBS said the dollar had been well bid since the first of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimonies to Congress last Wednesday. Greenspan said a pre-emptive interest rate rise could not be ruled out and this sent U.S. long-term yields sharply higher.
German yields have not followed suit because labour market concerns there mean the Bundesbank is not likely to raise interest rates any time soon.
A bigger than expected rise in the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management's February business activity index on Monday underlined the relatively brisk pace of U.S. growth, analysts said.
The second leg of Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins will be delivered on Wednesday, while the Fed chairman was also due to testify to the house budget committee at 1500 GMT on Tuesday.
On Wall Street overnight the Dow Jones industrial average jumped 41.18 points to 6,918.92 after losing more than 160 points over the previous three sessions.

European bourses responded with relief. London shares started higher and the blue chip FTSE 100 index soon put on more than three-quarters of a percent, moving within 20 points of its all-time high of 4,362.4, set on 20 February.

"Rates are not going up in the UK before the election and a small rise in the U.S. will be taken in the market's stride," one dealer said. "The only thing that could kill this raging bull is a clear sign of higher (U.S.) inflation -- and there is just no sign."
Provided Greenspan does not drop any bombshells on Wednesday and the U.S. jobs data on Friday is in line with expectations, the FTSE could head up to the 4,400 level soon, dealers said.

In Frankfurt Germany's DAX index pushed into new record territory above 3,300 points, boosted by the strength of the dollar -- which makes exports more attractive. A rally in the car sector following bullish noises from Daimler on its 1996 and 1997 results.
However, dealers were still wary ahead of Greenspan's next pronouncements.

On the Paris bourse the bulls were also rampant. French shares opened with a near one percent jump and then moved more than 1.5 percent higher on the back of the firm dollar and resurgent Wall Street.

"Everything is looking fine. Confidence is coming back while we are awaiting the U.S. statistics at the end of the week. As long as the dollar holds up, there is no reason why the market should fall," a broker said.
CURRENCIES AT NOON GMT
The dollar was at 1.7080 marks and 121.80 yen, compared with 1.6941 and 120.92 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT NOON GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 36.6 points at 4,343.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 39.44 points at 2,640.15.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 53.59 points at 3,317.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $361.75 compared with London's previous close of $362.25. Silver was at $5.29.
